items.title: OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms
items.summary: The firm used unreleased models to tackle hundreds of high-profile problems.

items.title: Cryo-EM structure of a methanogen nitrogenase–PII protein supercomplex
items.summary: Cryo-electron microscopy of a nitrogenase supercomplex from a methane-producing archaeon reveals a mechanism in which PII proteins drive assembly of such structures to regulate nitrogenase activity in response to nitrogen availability.

items.title: Can your brain grow new neurons? How researchers are solving a century-old puzzle
items.summary: Scientists have debated for decades whether the human brain sprouts new neurons throughout life. What would it mean if it could — and how much evidence is enough?

items.title: Australia’s current wildfire crisis linked to colonial land-use change
items.summary: A 1,000-year lake-sediment record from southeastern Australia shows that colonial disruption of Indigenous cultural burning transformed open woodland into dense, flammable forest, priming the landscape for today’s climate-driven wildfires.

items.title: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
items.summary: Byteification is a general method for retrofitting large language models to operate over bytes such that they approach the capabilities of subword-based systems and may be better for scientific data.

items.title: Retrofitted LLM can count the letter ‘i’s in ‘artificial intelligence’
items.summary: Most LLMs cannot reliably evaluate text on the level of individual letters. A technique called byteification retrofits existing models to enable it.

items.title: Australia’s bush fires got worse after British colonization — this is why
items.summary: The suppression of Indigenous burning practices probably spurred the growth of flammable forests.

items.title: Chemistry Nobel for solving mystery of how ‘handed’ organic molecules can emerge
items.summary: Prize awarded to two chemists who probed why life favours one mirror-image molecule over another.

items.title: A Jurassic mammaliaform swimmer and transformation of the mammalian pharynx
items.summary: A swimming and water-foraging mammaliaform, Megacauda sungei gen. et sp. nov., had a lifestyle analogous to the extant platypus, and was capable of mammal-like swallowing and suckling.

items.title: Woody ‘blankets’ are being deployed on Arctic permafrost to reduce carbon emissions
items.summary: A start-up company is testing whether stabilizing areas of rapidly eroding permafrost can prevent greenhouse-gas emissions.

items.title: Nuclear clocks tick for the first time
items.summary: Ultraprecise clocks that use transitions in atomic nuclei to keep time show promise as a next-generation time standard and for probing fundamental physics.

items.title: An early predecessor to mammals could swim, suckle and swallow
items.summary: A fossil of an early ancestor of mammals from the Jurassic period reveals a mammal-like throat passage (pharynx) and throat bones (hyoids). It fills a gap in our knowledge about throat features in the animals from which modern mammals evolved their ability to swallow as adults and suckle milk as babies.

items.title: A nuclear clock synchronized to <sup>229</sup>Th
items.summary: A nuclear clock synchronized to 229Th establishes laser-addressed nuclei as operational clock references and 229Th:CaF2 as a stable, reproducible solid-state platform for compact nuclear clocks and nuclear quantum sensors.

items.title: Prehistoric global migration of vanishing gut microbes with humans
items.summary: Microbial species disappearing from industrialized populations have evolved with humans over millennia and migrated worldwide with them—this may have consequences for human health.

items.title: Overcoming key challenges in the evolutionary transition to multicellularity
items.summary: This Review synthesizes an evolutionary framework for understanding the key stages, challenges and microevolutionary processes through which single cells evolve into functionally integrated multicellular organisms.

items.title: A split attractor design for rapidly writing a navigational goal
items.summary: The recurrent h∆K–PFG neural circuit generates persistent heading memories through slow excitation, fast inhibition and a disinhibitory gate, where disinhibition controls the functional coupling of the network to rapidly transition between measurement and memory.

items.title: A gut microbial odd-chain fatty acid alleviates atherosclerosis in mice
items.summary: The administration of Bacteroides uniformis in mice can mitigate atherosclerosis via pentadecanoic acid, which directly inhibits HMG-CoA reductase to promote hepatic cholesterol clearance.

items.title: Genome accessibility reveals disease risk that gene expression misses
items.summary: Most disease-associated genetic alterations do not affect the genes themselves, but instead change how strongly they are expressed, often by modifying genome accessibility. Gene expression and accessibility have now been analysed simultaneously in 10 million immune cells from 1,108 people, linking disease-associated changes in accessibility to gene expression.

items.title: A thorium-229 optical nuclear clock with feedback loop
items.summary: A thorium-229 nuclear clock is realized by stabilizing a continuous-wave laser to the 148-nm nuclear excitation with a rapid feedback loop based on absorption spectroscopy.

items.title: A preinvasive regulatory T cell axis for lung cancer interception
items.summary: An effector regulatory T cell circuit is identified that can be monitored in blood samples to track the development of lung cancer, and blockade of this immune network in the preinvasive setting can intercept tumorigenesis to reduce tumour incidence and size.

items.title: Dynamics of human cardiogenesis and its disruption in trisomy 21
items.summary: Single-cell and spatial multiomics are combined to define niches in the developing human heart, revealing pacemaker-cell organization, cardiomyocyte maturation and compaction, and developmental perturbations associated with trisomy 21.

items.title: Human lung organoid modelling of tissue-resident antiviral T cell responses
items.summary: Lung organoids containing endogenous resident immune cells show that SARS-CoV-2 infection elicits protective, tissue-resident memory T cell responses, demonstrating local recall immunity and providing a platform for the study of human tissue-resident antiviral defence.

items.title: Nobel prizes 2026: ‘ghost’ particles, mirror molecules and light switches in the brain
items.summary: Nature rounds up the Nobel prizes for science — plus, hints of the ancestral human gut microbiome.

items.title: Gut microbes that trace ancient human journeys
items.summary: The Indigenous African Hadza and South American Tsimane share gut microorganisms that shed light on human dispersals and microbial losses in industrialized societies.

items.title: Revealed: how this common gut microbe protects against heart disease
items.summary: Intestinal bacterium secretes a molecule that reduces cholesterol production, according to a mouse study.

items.title: RNA catalysis emerges from dynamic structural ensembles
items.summary: RNase P RNA forms shifting active and inactive conformers whose catalytic activity depends on Mg2+-driven tertiary-interaction dynamics, which are modulated by binding of accessory proteins.

items.title: Alveolar stem cells transdifferentiate to drive bronchiolar regeneration
items.summary: Identification of a cross-compartmental cellular mechanism for bronchiolar epithelial repair informs therapeutic strategies for airway injury.

items.title: Mechanism of spliceosome termination
items.summary: A coordinated sequence of RNA helicases and associated factors dismantles normal and defective spliceosome complexes to enable intron degradation and ensure accurate gene expression.

items.title: tRNA dosage regulates lineage dependency and resistance in prostate cancer
items.summary: A tRNA-specific regulatory pathway is associated with codon biology, lineage transitions and therapy resistance in prostate cancer.

items.title: Observation of critical topological phase transition
items.summary: Using an acoustic metamaterial platform, a critical topological phase transition is experimentally demonstrated establishing a hierarchical phase transition organization, in which topology shapes criticality beyond the conventional Landau–Ginzburg paradigm and standard topological phase transitions.

items.title: UAE completes Arab world's first solo space probe – and sets course for an asteroid
items.summary: The device will be launched on a joint UAE-US-built craft. Some researchers say it could be the last mission constructed with outside help.

items.title: Semiconductors pushed into insulator territory
items.summary: A material that was previously assumed to be an electrical insulator has been shown to be a semiconductor, with potential uses in electronics and optics.

items.title: Observation of relativistic bond weakening in seaborgium hexacarbonyl
items.summary: Gas chromatography analysis of compounds formed by the superheavy element seaborgium shows that the hexacarbonyl complex Sg(CO)6 exhibits lower first bond dissociation energy than the lighter chemical homologue W(CO)6, owing to relativistic bond weakening effects.

items.title: Hydrogen bonding in water under extreme confinement
items.summary: A new technique allows direct nanoscale observations of the vibrational response of water confined inside carbon nanotubes, revealing that high degrees of confinement disrupt the hydrogen bond network through a fluctuating and highly-dispersed molecular state.

items.title: Experimental observation of critical topology
items.summary: Experimental evidence indicating that critical gapless topological states can be characterized by the entanglement spectrum and wavefunctions is presented, demonstrating persistence of topology at phase boundaries and extension to higher-dimensional systems.

items.title: A 7-eV bandgap semiconductor based on silicon-doped α-(AlxGa1−x)2O3
items.summary: Suboxide molecular-beam epitaxy is used to grow silicon-doped α-(AlxGa1−x)2O3 films with bandgaps exceeding 7.0 eV, enabling the fabrication of a Schottky diode and a field-effect transistor with colossal-bandgap channels.

items.title: A chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological antiferromagnetism
items.summary: A chiral superlattice in collinear antiferromagnetic UOTe generates large Berry curvature and spin-polarized currents, enabling anomalous Hall effects and advancing chiral quantum materials for spintronics.

items.title: Spatially deterministic nucleation of 2D semiconductors by etching flux
items.summary: Etching-flux-mediated single-centred nucleation of two-dimensional semiconductors is used to deterministically localize a single nucleation event, expanding semiconductor deposition from controlling where materials grow to controlling where and how crystals can begin to form.

items.title: How to control where semiconductor crystals start growing
items.summary: Semiconductor crystals grow from tiny nuclei, but the position of these nuclei is difficult to control precisely and can affect the crystal’s properties. An approach using ‘etching flux’ has now been developed that constrains the position at which a nucleus forms, enabling spatially programmable growth of large single crystals of semiconducting material.

items.title: ‘When prevention disappears, infections rise’: can the world still end AIDS?
items.summary: The United Nations’ deadline for eliminating HIV/AIDS as a public-health threat is unlikely to be met. But medical, political and social advances have raised hopes that longer-term success is still possible.

items.title: Structural basis for regulating lipopolysaccharide transmembrane transport
items.summary: Structures of the protein machinery in Gram-negative bacteria that transports lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the cytoplasmic membrane to the outer leaflet of the outer membrane reveal how conformational changes in response to the presence of LPS promote its transport.

items.title: 5-oxoETE links redox control of epithelial damage detection and resilience
items.summary: The DHRS7–OXER1 pathway links oxidative stress to immunity and tissue resilience by modulating 5-oxoETE via NADP+–NADPH, activating OXER1 to recruit antimicrobial cells and induce NUDIX enzymes that protect epithelial redox integrity.

items.title: NASA releases trove of Moon data from historic Artemis II flight
items.summary: Annotated images and more collected by the four astronauts could inform missions to the lunar surface.

items.title: Why we must advocate for proper care on the frontlines of the Ebola outbreak
items.summary: As the Bundibugyo virus public-health crisis continues to evolve, physician Richard Kojan is finding ways to care for people with the infection and helping relatives to visit loved ones safely.

items.title: The science of superintelligence and why AI is still a useful word
items.summary: President Donald Trump wants to replace ‘artificial intelligence’ with ‘Super Intelligence’ — but there are questions about whether we’re there yet.

items.title: Why sound, strong science alone isn’t enough in pandemic preparedness
items.summary: Comparable data are key to protecting the world from the next epidemic, says bioengineer Polina Brangel.

items.title: How we ditched presentations and embraced silence in our lab meetings
items.summary: Swapping to a system in which lab members read memos quietly before team discussions helped to create an open culture.

items.title: A guide to Nature Index tables
items.summary: Information on the methodology used in the ranking for the 2026 Nature Spotlight: Infectious diseases.

items.summary: Author Correction: Anodic Pd membrane H 2 extraction enhances thermochemical dehydrogenation
